sum: U.S. travel stocks surged on Wednesday, November 4, as airlines, cruise operators, and online booking companies rallied after the 2026 midterm elections.

Shares of Expedia, Booking Holdings and several major airlines recorded strong gains as oil prices fell sharply amid investor expectations that the election results could increase pressure for an end to the war with Iran.

The gains followed Democratic victories in both chambers of Congress, changing the political balance in Washington. Investors responded to the possibility that a shift in U.S. policy could help ease geopolitical tensions and energy costs, although there has been no confirmed change in the administration’s approach to the conflict.
Online travel companies were among the strongest performers during Wednesday’s trading session.
Shares of Expedia Group climbed 10.54% to close at $315.88, while Booking Holdings, the parent company of Booking.com, gained 9.83% to $170.97. Airbnb advanced 5.64% to $176.37.

According to Dow Jones Newswires, travel stocks benefited from growing investor expectations that the election outcome could help bring an end to the Iran war, which has created significant challenges for travel companies.

Higher fuel expenses have forced airlines to raise fares and reduce capacity, while cruise operators have faced additional operating costs. Travel companies have also reported pressure on consumer spending, with some travelers choosing shorter trips or destinations closer to home.

sum: New Delhi, Nov. 3 -- Reliance Industries share price: Reliance Industries share price declined over 1% in intraday trade on Tuesday, November 3, on profit booking after rallying nearly 12% in the previous session. The stock fell as much as 1.3% to an intraday low of Rs.1,281.55 on the NSE, giving back some of Monday's sharp gains.

Reliance Industries shares had surged 11.6% on Monday to close at Rs.1,300, their highest level since early September. The rally marked the stock's biggest single-day gain since April 2020 and helped lift the Nifty 50 by 1.7%, given the company's heavyweight presence in the index.

The sharp rebound also added Rs.1.84 lakh crore to Reliance Industries' market capitalisation, taking it to Rs.17.6 lakh crore and helping it retain its position as India's most valuable listed company. At its peak of Rs.1,611, the company had commanded a market capitalisation of Rs.21.8 lakh crore. It had crossed the Rs.21 lakh crore milestone in June 2024, becoming the first Indian company to achieve the feat.

Despite Monday's rally, Reliance shares remain down 17.22% so far in 2026. The stock had been under pressure for much of the year, closing lower in eight of the previous 10 months. The latest gains followed the company's record quarterly profit, which renewed investor interest in the stock.

Reliance Industries reported a record consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of Rs.29,550 crore for Q2FY27, marking a 33.8% increase from Rs.22,092 crore in the year-ago quarter. Revenue rose 27.8% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs.3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record Rs.62,409 crore.

The oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business was the biggest contributor to the strong performance. Its EBITDA surged 67.9% to Rs.25,203 crore, supported by higher global fuel margins and improved petrochemical spreads. O2C revenue increased 44.2% to Rs.2,31,601 crore, with supply disruptions in West Asia and other regions pushing transportation fuel cracks higher.

Digital services also supported earnings, while retail remained a relative weak spot. Reliance Retail Ventures reported a 24.3% decline in PAT to Rs.2,611 crore, despite a 6.4% rise in revenue to Rs.91,716 crore. Its EBITDA, before a one-time impairment charge, fell 8.6% to Rs.6,228 crore.

Can Booking Holdings Stock Jump 40%?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Shares of Booking Holdings (BKNG) have lost 26.4% over the past year, while the S&P 500 returned 11.3%. For the stock to climb 40% from here, the company must be a sound business navigating a spell of pressure on travel, rather than one that has stopped delivering. In five of the last ten calendar years, the stock climbed 40% or more at some point within the year. The shares now trade at 15.8 times earnings, compared with 22.6 for the median S&P 500 company. Is that low price backed by a business that is still earning more?

Yes, so far. Operating profit reached $9.74 billion in the twelve months to June 2026, up from $8.22 billion a year earlier. Fiscal Q2 2026 operating profit also increased, rising to $2.5 billion from $2.25 billion. Over those twelve months, the company posted an operating margin of 34.5%, compared with 18.7% for the median S&P 500 company.

The company sells room nights, flight tickets and attraction tickets to travelers. Room nights grew 5% in fiscal Q2 2026, topping management’s guidance. Free cash flow held up too, totaling $9.54 billion over the twelve months to June 2026, against $9.24 billion a year earlier. So the discount is on profit and cash that are still growing.

Management points to the conflict in the Middle East: on its August 4, 2026 call, it said higher airline prices and reduced flight capacity kept long-haul international travel under pressure. Fiscal Q2 2026 revenue grew 8.1%, about half the 16.2% rate from the prior quarter. International room nights rose only slightly, while domestic room nights grew high single digits.

Over the twelve months to June 2026, the slowdown looks smaller. Revenue grew 12.9%, compared with an average of 13.5% for the last three twelve-month periods, this one included. Management expects slower growth still, guiding revenue growth of 4% to 6% for fiscal Q3 2026 on the assumption that the conflict’s effects on flights last through that quarter. The company also lowered its full-year gross bookings expectation, mainly because of slower flight ticket growth.
Not all of the pressure comes from the conflict.

Why Booking (BKNG) stock is down today
sum: Shares of online travel agency Booking Holdings BKNG fell 3.8% in the afternoon session after the European Commission initiated formal proceedings to determine whether the company breached the Digital Services Act.

The European Commission announced that the inquiry evaluates whether Booking.com adequately assessed and mitigated risks from fake listings and phishing scams. Additionally, the regulatory body is examining whether the platform failed to clearly label paid search rank placements as advertisements. Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen emphasized that European consumers require protection from fraudulent practices when booking holidays, noting that the Digital Services Act imposes specific responsibilities on leading services. Heightened regulatory scrutiny introduces legal uncertainty, raising investor concern over potential penalties and required adjustments to the platform's European operations.
After the initial drop, the shares shed some of the losses and rose to $158.11, down 3.6% from the previous close.

Booking’s shares are somewhat volatile and have had 14 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 29 days ago when the stock dropped 4.1% on the news that the rapid adoption of Meta’s new autonomous AI assistant, Muse, sparked concerns over structural disruption to digital marketplaces and digital advertising revenues.

Booking is down 25.8% since the beginning of the year, and at $158.11 per share, it is trading 28% below its 52-week high of $219.68 from January 2026. What Could Lift Booking Holdings Stock?
sum: Shares of Booking Holdings (BKNG) have lost 17.2% over the past year, lagging the S&P 500 and its 17.4% return. Following that decline, the stock trades at 17.3 times earnings. That multiple sits below the company’s average of 28.3 over its last 12 fiscal quarter ends. A lower P/E means paying less for each dollar of profit, but that discount only pays off if the profit keeps growing. So what would have to go right for Booking Holdings stock to climb from here?

Selling more travel would generate most of the stock’s potential gain. Under Trefis’s three-year scenario, higher revenue accounts for 82.4% of the upside. That means more room nights, the nights travelers book through platforms like Booking.com, alongside more flight and attraction tickets. Following these assumptions, the stock would appreciate about 49% in three years, excluding dividends.
The table compares Booking Holdings today against the scenario three years out.

An expanding multiple provides a further 28.4% of the upside, assuming a higher P/E, while a lower margin takes 10.8% back. This scenario lifts the P/E from 17.3 to 19.4. Even after that increase, the multiple would remain below the stock’s own 12-quarter average of 28.3.

The scenario models revenue growth of 11.6% a year. That pace falls slightly behind the 12.9% Booking Holdings delivered over the twelve months to fiscal Q2 2026. Growth slowed in the latest quarter, so the scenario needs the pace to pick up again as travelers book more nights and more of the rest of their trips through the company’s sites. Room nights increased 5% and revenue rose 8% in fiscal Q2 2026, management said on the August 4, 2026 call. Executives issued a slower guide for the following period, forecasting fiscal Q3 2026 revenue growth of 4% to 6%. However, that guidance covers a single quarter rather than three years, and it assumes the conflict in the Middle East keeps weighing on long-haul travel.

Booking Holdings is also capturing more business from its most loyal customers. Members of its Genius levels 2 and 3 accounted for more than 30% of active customers in fiscal Q2 2026, representing an increase from a year earlier. Management also said that trips combining several bookings grew more than twice as fast as total transactions at Booking.com.

sum: Carnival stock just posted a gain that crushed every rival cruise line and left the broader market in the dust, but record 2027 bookings cut both ways for anyone deciding what to do with their shares right now.

That kind of run forces a decision for anyone holding the shares. Locking in a quick gain has obvious appeal. Yet the booking data behind the rally speaks to revenue that extends well past the quarter Carnival just reported. Record 2027 bookings at Carnival sit at the center of both arguments.
Both sides of that decision have real support. The lead Carnival stock holds over its rivals argues for patience, while the stock’s incomplete recovery across 2026 argues for caution.

Carnival reported its Q3 2026 results in late September and stated that bookings for 2027 had reached record levels. That announcement started the month-long climb in Carnival shares. Chief executive Josh Weinstein weighed in. He declared in the earnings release, “We delivered another quarter of top and bottom-line records, with accelerating demand and even stronger cost discipline driving results ahead of our expectations.”

Because Carnival sells cabins well ahead of sailing, next year’s bookings say more about its revenue than the quarter just reported. The record 2027 bookings offer an early read on revenue Carnival hasn’t yet recognized, giving that number unusual weight in how Carnival stock gets valued.

Carnival stock’s lead over two cruise rivals is what makes this run notable. At the same time, Royal Caribbean Group (NYSE:RCL) stock is up 10% to $279.58 over the past month. That solid advance still trails Carnival stock.

Booking Holdings (BKNG) closed at $180.30 on September 8, down 6.72% on a day the S&P 500 barely moved, swept up in a travel-sector selloff after gasoline futures spiked on renewed Middle East tensions. The tape was macro noise. The more useful thing happened hours earlier, when CEO Glenn Fogel sat on stage at Citi’s Global TMT Conference and dismantled the exact fear that has kept this stock cheap all year.

Booking now trades at roughly 16 times next-twelve-month earnings, per TIKR, near the low end of its 52-week range and well under its own five-year forward average of about 20 times. The market’s two worries are the Middle East drag on long-haul travel and the idea that AI chatbots will eventually route travelers around online travel agencies. Fogel spent his Citi appearance arguing the second fear misreads what actually protects this business.

Asked what proprietary data defends Booking’s role in discovery, Fogel gave a startling answer for a CEO: “I’ve been here 27 years. There’s almost no proprietary data of any kind.” His point was that the moat was never a hoard of data an AI could scrape. It is the working relationship with partners, the live and accurate inventory, and the trust that money is safe and problems get fixed, coordinated globally in a way he argued no rival matches.

If the edge were a static database, a large language model with an API could threaten it. Because the edge is execution and a two-sided marketplace, the AI question becomes who deploys it best, and Booking is deploying it aggressively. Fogel described running five parallel AI efforts at once, including two greenfield teams told to “pretend you’re not part of the company and start something fresh,” one led by KAYAK founder Steve Hafner. He called AI “a prediction machine” that should flag a rainy museum day and rebook your itinerary before you notice. On the cost side, he said AI has already driven a double-digit reduction in customer-service costs while satisfaction rose.

The sharp fall came as investors booked profits after the stock's massive rally over the past year. Bajaj Consumer shares have gained nearly 150 percent in 2026 and around 190 percent over the last one year, making it one of the best-performing FMCG stocks.

Operating performance also improved significantly. EBITDA more than doubled to Rs 83.4 crore from Rs 41 crore in the same quarter last year, while net profit increased to Rs 70.7 crore, reflecting better margins and higher sales.

The company's flagship Almond Drops Hair Oil (ADHO) continued to drive growth. The domestic ADHO business recorded growth in the 30 percent range, while underlying volume growth remained in the early teens. Sachets and lower price-point packs continued to perform better than the overall brand.
Bajaj Consumer also reported high-20 percent year-on-year growth in its general trade business during the quarter, indicating strong demand across traditional retail channels.

Despite the healthy numbers, investors appeared cautious about future growth. After the sharp rally in the stock, many market participants chose to lock in profits following the earnings announcement.
